$comment: The three analytic surface loads of Spada et al. (2011), table 4. Each is an axisymmetric surface mass density as a function of colatitude from the load centre, with a closed form for its Legendre coefficients. Mass conservation is not applied: these expressions describe the load alone, and no compensating ocean load exists in that benchmark.

source.citation: Spada, G. et al. (2011). Geophysical Journal International 185(1), 106-132, tables 2 and 4.

constants.$comment: Table 2. The ice density of 931 kg/m3 and the water density of 1000 kg/m3 differ from the GIAMIP values of 917 and 1025; a shared constants module would give one of the two the other's numbers.

cap.name: Spherical cap, parabolic cross-section
cap.surface_mass_density: sigma(theta) = rho_ice * h * sqrt((cos(theta) - cos(alpha)) / (1 - cos(alpha))) for 0 <= theta <= alpha, and 0 beyond
cap.legendre_coefficients: sigma_n = -rho_ice*h/(4*(1-cos(alpha))) * [ (T_{n+1}(alpha) - T_{n+2}(alpha))/(n + 3/2) - (T_{n-1}(alpha) - T_n(alpha))/(n - 1/2) ], for n >= 1, where T_n(alpha) = cos(n*alpha) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind as defined in table 2
cap.note: This is the load Martinec et al. (2018) reuse for every one of their five cases.

disc.name: Disc, rectangular cross-section
disc.surface_mass_density: sigma(theta) = rho_ice * h for 0 <= theta <= alpha, and 0 beyond
disc.legendre_coefficients: sigma_n = rho_ice*h/2 * [ -P_{n+1}(cos alpha) + P_{n-1}(cos alpha) ], for n >= 1

placement.test_3_2: Centroid at colatitude 25 degrees, longitude 75 degrees.

time_history.description: A Heaviside step: the load is applied at t = 0 and held. Geodetic quantities are evaluated at t = 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 and infinity kyr.

output_grids.harmonic_degrees: n_min = 2 to n_max = 128 for the viscoelastic normal mode results of tests 1/2 and 2/2
